segment_text: (a)Rolling Forecast. At least ** before the ** of each Calendar Quarter during the Term of this Supply Agreement, Kissei shall provide Rigel a rolling forecast of its monthly requirements for the quantity of Products to be used for (i) Development purposes for the following ** period commencing from such Calendar Quarter and (ii) Commercial use for the following ** period commencing from such Calendar Quarter (“Order Forecast”). For clarity, each Order Forecast shall itemize the applicable quantity (i.e., the unit of Drum or naked bottle, but not limited to such unit) of the Product and its placebo (if applicable) for each of Development and Commercial use. Each Order Forecast shall be made in good faith for budget and capacity planning purposes only and shall be non-binding on Kissei and Rigel, except as provided in Section 2.2(b). The Parties shall discuss and review the Order Forecast at each regularly scheduled meeting of the JSC established by the Parties under the Collaboration and License Agreement (or by a subcommittee established by the JSC to oversee the manufacture and supply of the Product). The Order Forecast will be in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit B.

annotator_notes:
Redaction is the EMBEDDED shape (section 3.7.1): the clause survives and establishes that a lead-time deadline exists; only its values are withheld, so known_gap=redacted_value, not redacted_clause. Reviewer ruled the segment holds THREE obligation-bearing clauses [CORRECTED 2026-08-22 (B3): TWO, not three -- the 'itemize' clause was excluded on a non-party subject and the reviewer confirmed that exclusion; see batch01/exclusions.json E03-005#itemize] (provide / itemize / discuss-and-review), with 'shall be non-binding' and 'will be in substantially the form' read as status characterisations rather than duties -- so the segment is eligible under section 2's 1-3 band and yields three items. This is the first. Note the temporal would fail even unredacted: the underlying obligation is recurring-with-lead-time, plausibly EVERY composed with RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER, which IR v1 cannot represent (section 7 composition gap). Both parties are named and should resolve to real PartyRefs, unlike item E01-01.

CLAUSE-COUNT CORRECTION 2026-08-22 (B3): this segment yields TWO obligation-bearing clauses, not three. The original eligibility ruling assumed three (provide / itemize / discuss-and-review); 'itemize' has a document as its grammatical subject and was excluded, confirmed by the reviewer, and 'discuss-and-review' was excluded as cross-reference-dependent. The segment remains eligible under §2's 1-3 band either way. Correction recorded rather than silently edited, per this project's corrections-are-new-text discipline.

SECOND GAP TAGGED 2026-09-18 (F19, guideline v0.61, §8.11): known_gaps gains lead_time_unrepresentable. The note above is RIGHT that the temporal would fail even unredacted -- confirmed through the real compile_candidate(), which returns UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL for both the redacted phrase as emitted and a plausible unredacted one -- and WRONG about why. It is NOT a §7 composition gap. §7's gap is EVERY+DURING, where each operand IS an available form and only their co-occurrence fails; here neither claimed operand is available for this text (Duration has no UNRESOLVED alias variant, so 'each Calendar Quarter' has no form; RelativeToTriggerTemporal has no duration slot, so 'at least ** before' has no form), and the note omits 'during the Term' entirely, which is §7's actual operand. The decisive test: granting free composition of all five v1 forms does NOT rescue this clause, because composition joins whole forms and NO form pairs a duration with a direction. So the gap is single-form expressiveness, not composition -- hence a tag of its own rather than a composition tag. Direction INCOMPLETENESS, reached independently of the note. STAMP DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at v0.28: known_gaps is not one of §5's eight scored clauses, so this cannot change how the item scores, and restamping was MEASURED to move the published all-items figure 5/15 = 33.3% -> 5/14 = 35.7% purely by staling E03-005's cassettes and dropping this PARTIAL item out of the denominator -- a figure improving for no improvement. Same refusal as C11-01's v0.52 record-only correction. See holdout/E03_01_TEMPORAL_INVESTIGATION.md.

THIRD GAP TAGGED 2026-09-23 (F21, guideline v0.63, §8.12): known_gaps gains temporal_composition, and this item was NOT among the two logged instances that forced the amendment -- it was swept in by §8.11's own observation that the F19 note 'omits during the Term entirely'. That omission is not merely a defect in the note: 'during the Term of this Supply Agreement' is a SECOND temporal element, bounding how long the quarterly forecast duty subsists, and IR v1's ast.Obligation carries ONE temporal field, so it cannot be held alongside the lead-time element whatever is done about the latter. THE TWO TAGS ARE DISTINCT AND NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER: lead_time_unrepresentable (§8.11) says the lead-time element has NO v1 form at all -- single-form expressiveness, which free composition would not rescue; temporal_composition (§8.12) says that even granting a form for every element, only one of them can reach the slot. §9's per-tag counts are already non-summable and say so. DIRECTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSIGNED for the new tag (F21): dropping 'during the Term' leaves the IR claiming the duty runs forever, which is OVERSTATING-shaped, where this item's own lead_time tag is INCOMPLETENESS -- the divergence inside one item is part of what F21 asks. STAMP DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at v0.28, on F19's own precedent and for its own measured reason: known_gaps is not one of §5's eight scored clauses, and restamping would stale E03-005's three cassettes and drop a scored PARTIAL item out of the all-items denominator -- a figure improving for no improvement. Confirmed by a real run_scoring.run() before and after: no published figure moves.
